input_packet.case_brief:
Senior SWE with 12 years FAANG experience deciding among three job offers (FAANG staff+, Series B founding engineer, stay) within 7 days amid family and career plateau constraints.

Constraints stated during conversation:
- [ACTIVE] No clear path to staff at current company (explicit feedback, structural)
- [ACTIVE] 7-day decision deadline
- [ACTIVE] 80% base salary cut for Option B, 0.8% equity
- [ACTIVE] Family: wife physician (primary earner), two kids (7,4)
- [ACTIVE] Financially survivable for Option B (mortgage fine, modest cuts)

Original framing: User presents three job options (A: FAANG staff+ 15% comp bump; B: Series B founding eng 80% base cut +0.8% equity; C: stay) with 7-day deadline, current FAANG plateau, family (wife, two kids); assumes equal weighting, seeks help picking.

step6_output.answer_core:
You are not making a single seven-day choice among three static labels. Run this as a sequenced process to avoid a forced error.

Step 1: Ask all three companies for a deadline extension. At staff level, most will grant a few days; you need breathing room.

Step 2: Have the conversation with your wife before you do deep startup due diligence. The 80% base cut and 0.8% equity only make sense if there is genuine joint buy-in on what “modest cuts” means for a family with a 7- and 4-year-old while she is the primary earner. If she is not fully in, eliminate Option B now.

Step 3: If you have alignment at home, negotiate two things with the Series B before committing: a six-month compensation ramp and remote/hybrid boundaries that protect family time. In parallel, verify runway length, CEO quality through back-channel references, and whether the 0.8% is on a fully diluted basis—or get a credible dilution model. Do not treat the offer as final until those terms close.

Step 4: If the wife conversation says no, or if the startup due diligence surfaces red flags, take Option A. Treat it as a 24-month bridge: the staff+ title and 15% comp bump are real, but it is a delay, not a solution, to wanting to build something you own.

Step 5: Do not stay at your current company as a safe default. The structural block on staff means staying is an active choice to ride a declining plateau, and the distraction you feel will likely worsen.

Your decision tree: extensions → wife gate → (if yes) negotiate B + diligence → (if no/red flags) take A → reject C as a passive default.
